To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the false-alarm rate for gravitational wave bursts was 4 h−1 for a gravitational wave amplitude of 3 × 1017 and that this false-alarm rate was caused by non-Gausian noise.
the analysis of 1000 hours of data did not find any evidence of detection, and the false-alarm rate was 4 events/h.
no gravitational waves were found in TAMA300 data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a search for gravitational waves with a detector of a 300 m laser interferometer.
a search for gravitational wave bursts with the TAMA300 detector.
the detection and characterization of gravitational waves, with a particular focus on the development of data analysis algorithms and the application of these to the data from TAMA300.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we did not detect any gravitational waves in the 1000 h data, but that we did detect some non-Gaussian noises.
the sensitivity of our burst search analysis is about h ~ 3 x 10-17 for a 1 ms burst signal.
no evidence of a signal was found, and no evidence of noise was found either.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a limit of h ~ 3.3 × 10-17 for a gravitational wave burst with a frequency of 1000 Hz and a duration of 0.1 ms.
we could not detect any gravitational waves, but we have improved the detector sensitivity and the analysis methods.
we have developed a new analysis method and applied it to a large amount of real data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we developed a data analysis method that is applicable to short bursts of gravitational wave signals.
we have shown the importance of the time-dependence analysis for the rejection of the non-Gaussian noise.
the excess power filter can be used for the detection of gravitational waves.
